subject: mangoes packed in neat rows and columns in a wholesale fruit market, with one extra row being laid along the edge
why: the chapter opener: a product is a rectangle of rows and columns, so adding one row or one column grows it by a whole column or row, which is the distributive property in a crate
gemini_prompt: Documentary photograph of a wholesale mango market in India in early morning light: large shallow wooden trays on a stall, each holding ripe yellow and green mangoes packed in a perfect rectangular grid of rows and columns, and beside one tray a single extra straight row of mangoes laid along its long edge, as if the tray is being made one row bigger, jute sacks and stacked empty crates in the soft background, natural colours, shallow depth of field. No text, no numerals, no signs, no labels, no logos, no people anywhere in the frame.
